subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable batching/aggregation of outbound Telegram notifications

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in outbound Telegram notification digest policy, and should that policy live in the Telegram plugin, shared outbound delivery, or an external plugin/hook surface?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-backed, but the permanent contract affects config shape, delivery timing, urgent error bypass, media/thread semantics, persistence, and the plugin-versus-shared delivery boundary.

options.title: Define opt-in durable digest policy
options.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush behavior before implementation.

options.title: Require external plugin or hook extension
options.body: Keep core lean and extend or document plugin hooks only if durable delayed aggregation cannot be built safely with current surfaces.

options.title: Keep immediate delivery semantics
options.body: Treat current streaming coalescing, throttling, and error cooldowns as the supported anti-spam mechanisms and narrow or close the request later.

recommendation.title: Define opt-in durable digest policy
recommendation.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has strong history across Telegram outbound behavior and shared channel-delivery policy seams.
